Result up front

3rounds to impeccable: States, Motion, UX
1round to Craft: Accessibility
4draws: Color, Type, Layout, Copy
4/4blind ship picks went to impeccable
  • Landing page: impeccable won clearly. Both judges gave it Layout, States, Motion and UX, and G counted 12 of 13 planted defects fixed against Craft's 7.
  • In-app screen: close. G gave Craft Layout and Accessibility and counted 9 of 12 fixes for Craft against impeccable's 7, yet both judges still chose to ship impeccable.
  • Copy is a draw. Craft's Copy mode is better-writing, and the blind judges found no instruction gap.
  • Direction: Craft refuses to fight, by design. impeccable built a whole new riso-zine direction unopposed.
  • Each cell is a single run, so read these as observed outcomes, not a ranking. See caveats.

Tale of the tape

Run as a Team Up Arena. Each skill was the only variable: both sides ran on Claude Opus 5.5, saw the same seed file and context, and wrote to isolated folders. Contestants were told to follow their skill's own loading rules and cite the rules they applied.

  1. 1 · AuditSix shards read every instruction file of both skills, checking line ranges, and built rule inventories with line citations. The first two codex auditors truncated their reads, so their work was discarded and redone.
  2. 2 · SeedsTwo flawed pages based on Creative Room, plus a hidden list of 25 skill-neutral planted defects, written before any run.
  3. 3 · FightSix runs: landing refine, in-app refine and new direction, once per skill. Non-interactive: no run could ask the user.
  4. 4 · Captureagent-browser screenshots at 1440 and 390, a Tab-focus shot, axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA, overflow, infinite-animation count and a reduced-motion pass.
  5. 5 · Blind judgesG (GPT-6.1 Sol, high) and M (Gemini 3.8 Flash, high) scored anonymised X/Y outputs per pillar against a written rubric. The mapping was sealed.
  6. 6 · Rule judgeUnblinded GPT-6.1 Sol combined the verdicts, preferring G's line-cited evidence, and tied each win to rules it checked in both skills' files. Six citations were then spot-checked by hand.

Why these tasks

  • Refine, don't build. atlas-craft only refines existing interfaces. A from-scratch build would score its refusal, not its craft. A shared flawed seed is where both skills actually overlap.
  • Landing vs in-app. impeccable treats them as different modes (Persuade vs Operate), and craft doesn't. The real Desk screen also tests empty, loading, error and destructive states that a landing page never shows.
  • A third, deliberately unfair task: "new visual direction". It exposes refusal behaviour instead of assuming it.
  • Real material: Creative Room's README, the Desk's real PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md, and gallery stills made by the studio's own tools. Creative Room's code was never touched.

Bonus stage · not counted in the 8 rounds

New visual direction

"The landing page feels generic. I want a new visual direction, not a tidy-up. Make it."

Team Craft

DOES NOT ENTERindex.html is byte-identical to the seed (cmp-verified)
"Declined to build. Atlas Craft refines an existing interface. It has no method for creating a new visual direction, and it says that a new direction needs its own decision." — contestant NOTES

Declined new-direction construction, also declined an unwanted tidy-up, and left index.html byte-identical to seeds/landing.orig/index.html (cmp verified). The supplied 390px metrics retain 1180px scroll width and the original accessibility/motion defects.

ContractConsistent with its narrow refinement contract and absence of a direction-selection method. SKILL.md:23 reserves a separate direction decision; it does not literally say never redesign or refuse a user who has already requested one, so the all-stop is a conservative benchmark interpretation reinforced by the ban on substituting general design knowledge, not a universal hard prohibition. Notes cite stale line 22; current verified line is 23.

impeccable

Built a replacement Three-Drum Riso Zine: full blue opening, pink/yellow ink vocabulary, Bricolage display, misregistration, textured floods, live deterministic canvas, Play/Pause, frame scrubber and drum toggles. Added inferred PRODUCT.md, six-block surface contract, token-bearing landing DESIGN.md and JSON sidecar.

QualityClear direction capability win: supplied desktop/mobile views show a distinctive, legible code-rendering demonstration and a visible command action. Source verifies multiply compositing, seeded dropout, frame controls, paused reduced-motion default and offscreen/hidden drawing guard; supplied metrics have no page overflow at 1440/390 and zero axe findings. This is screenshot/source judgment, not fresh runtime interaction or a claim of production readiness.

ContractSubstantially follows replacement-world, concept seed, contract and documentation instructions, but not fully: NOTES:54 says decision wait exited 3 and the build proceeded, whereas new-work.md:51 requires repeating exit 3 and reserves the unanswered fallback for exit 4. NOTES:25–27 describe inferred PRODUCT.md before the later decision-page attempt; init.md:31 requires probing an available decision page before inference. Review remains self-reported fix with one partial item, honestly disclosed rather than passed; scoped landing documentation preserves the Desk’s separate root system.

RisksThe supplied full-page screenshot still shows paper in the intended yellow creations and pink Desk regions, consistent with the reported open print-in issue; source’s awaiting cover depends on IntersectionObserver firing. Product audience and CTA remain inferred; pnpm desk:start precedes prerequisites. Clipboard failure only says Press ⌘C and has no live status region; the reduced-motion preference is read at startup rather than updated. A conventional copy-left/canvas-right hero limits how radical the composition is, even though the material and live mechanism are specific.

W/O

Walkover: IMPECCABLE

Impeccable wins direction task completion and demonstrated direction quality; Craft is out of scope / no submission, not a poor redesign. For an end-to-end direction-capability score count Craft as unfulfilled (zero completion), while any quality-only comparison marks Craft N/A and reports impeccable alone; report Craft’s scope adherence separately. Do not average this asymmetric scope test into the eight refinement pillars or excuse impeccable’s process deviations and open fix disposition.

Landing (Persuade)

  • impeccable 4 wins, 0 losses, 4 draws. Both judges gave it Layout, States, Motion and UX.
  • Decisive rule: Persuade's opening must "expose a clear action… in its working form" (mode-persuade.md:9). impeccable shipped a copyable pnpm desk:start, while Craft's "Start the Desk" scrolled.
  • Craft kept a three-card scaffold, which impeccable's craft-floor bans as page structure (craft-floor.md:25). Craft has no equivalent rule.
  • Color, type, a11y and copy were all near-identical: both reached 0 axe violations and identical contrast.

In-app (Operate)

  • Even on pillars: Craft won Layout and Accessibility, impeccable won States and Motion, four draws.
  • Craft's mechanical depth showed here: preserved accessible names, a 3:1 input boundary, a native dialog, and more planted defects fixed (9 vs 7 per G).
  • impeccable still won both ship picks: its states connect (retry settles), its error copy is product-true, and its loading respects reduced motion.
  • Craft's single biggest loss is an execution bug, not a missing rule: its retry deadlock goes against its own ui/index.md:13.

Where each one refuses to fight

Scope limits, routing to other skills and things to ask first, each cited to the line in the skill files.

Team Craft

  • New visual direction needs a separate decision; no direction-creation method is supplied. skills/atlas-craft/SKILL.md:23
  • Whole-interface audits/change reviews route to Atlas Review; substantial prose routes to Writing for Humans. skills/atlas-craft/SKILL.md:25
  • Domain handoffs do not require cross-discipline orchestration for ordinary refinement. skills/atlas-craft/references/ownership.md:5
  • States creates a workbench only on explicit request; ordinary state polish does not authorize rebuilding the Bench or removing it. skills/atlas-craft/SKILL.md:21
  • Contrast or palette changes require authorization; the refinement briefs already authorize these fixes. skills/atlas-craft/references/color/index.md:55
  • Do not introduce a new face unless asked for a type change. skills/atlas-craft/references/type/index.md:19
  • Ask between the two visually different iOS 16px input fixes; app contestant chose sizing up under non-interactive constraints. skills/atlas-craft/references/type/index.md:96
  • Reject animation failing frequency or purpose gates; this is a successful refusal, not a missing effect. skills/atlas-motion/references/animate/animate.md:45
  • Motion Opportunities is read-only, Performance diagnoses first, audits/reviews route to Atlas Review; React Native/Expo is excluded. skills/atlas-motion/SKILL.md:18

impeccable

  • Refinement preserves identity/behavior; redesign replaces the world but preserves product truth. SKILL.md:28
  • Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims; supplied refinement facts and non-interactive constraints explain the disclosed substitutions. SKILL.md:28
  • Polish must not conceal redesign; if the concept is wrong route to redesign or bolder. reference/polish.md:3
  • Audit reports and does not fix; web audit routes native platforms elsewhere. reference/audit.md:1
  • A new identity found during colorizing or typesetting routes through new-work rather than local refinement. reference/colorize.md:23
  • Missing PRODUCT blocks new/replacement work through init, but narrow existing refinements may proceed and offer init afterward. SKILL.md:77
  • Local extensions inherit identity and need approval before durable DESIGN.md changes. reference/new-work.md:33
  • Direction selection must run concept-seed and follow the decision-page answer/fallback contract; no silent skip. reference/new-work.md:48
  • No image generation means code-led, not a refused build; code-led skips comp round by contract. reference/new-work.md:55
  • Do not fabricate factual/commercial claims or unsupported capabilities. reference/new-work.md:59
  • Do not repair context drift as a design-task side effect. SKILL.md:88
  • Default scaffolds are refused; eyebrows are an absolute ban, while most other defaults can be earned by the brief. reference/craft-floor.md:21

In short: Craft won't pick a direction, and won't audit a whole interface or write long prose, which go to Atlas Review and Writing for Humans. impeccable won't polish over a wrong concept, and asks before replacing factual copy. It has no direction it refuses.

Honest caveats

Sample and setup

  • n = 1 per cell. One run per skill per task. G's own notes show single bugs swinging whole pillars (the retry deadlock, the hidden mobile names).
  • I wrote the seeds and the defect list. I wrote them skill-neutral and before any run, but a different seed would test different rules.
  • Home advantage. The Desk's real PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md were originally made with impeccable's schema. A schema comment was stripped from the judges' copy, but impeccable's context script reads exactly this format.
  • Non-interactive. Neither skill could ask the user. That penalises Craft's "needs its own decision" path most, and it also pushed impeccable off its decision-page contract (new-work.md:51).
  • Static stand-ins. These are single-file HTML pages, not the React Desk, so there's no real persistence. Both outputs claim saves they can't perform.

Judging

  • Judge M was lenient: it marked all 25 plants fixed for both skills. Where the judges split, the combined result favours G's line-cited evidence. With M alone, impeccable would win more pillars.
  • Model families: contestants were Claude, blind judges GPT and Gemini (to avoid self-preference), and the rule judge GPT. Some audit shards were Claude Sonnet after the codex reads truncated.
  • Blinding is partial. Judges didn't know the methods, but the two outputs differ in style. The direction round can't be blinded, because one side submitted nothing.
  • Equal weights for pillars and surfaces is a choice. The bonus round is reported separately, not averaged in.
  • No human judge, no screen reader, and no real-device test. Runtime checks were automated (axe, metrics, screenshots).

Rule judge's summary: On equal-weight refinement surfaces, color, typography, layout and copy tie; Craft wins accessibility, and impeccable wins states, motion and UX. G is preferred on disagreements because its evidence is more discriminating, while M marks every plant fixed and sometimes contradicts its own defects. Craft’s deeper mechanical instructions do not guarantee cleaner execution, and its Copy mode is better-writing. Impeccable alone demonstrates replacement-direction capability, with an open fix disposition and documented process deviations. These single runs establish observed outcomes and plausible rule links, not causal proof or a population-level ranking.
